notes: Site is hkliving.com (no dash) per prior-pass notes; reachable directly via HTTP, no robots.txt block. Checked: main nav mega-menu (Sofas/Furniture/Kitchen/Textile/Lighting/Accessories/Outdoor/Art/Brand kit/Add ons -- all plain category nodes, no Bestsellers item), footer nav, account/login area, and the site's dedicated collections index at /collection/ (title 'HKLIVING: Products'), which lists every named marketing collection: Must-haves, Collection 26-27, Additions 2026, 70s ceramics Van Gogh, Teun Zwets for HKLIVING, Nienke Sikkema for HKLIVING, Collection 25-26, New classics, HKLIVING x Gabriella Ferrero, Additions 2025, Collection 24-25, 70s ceramics collection. Only 'Must-haves' plausibly maps to a bestseller/popularity concept (English term is generic enough to be curated-favorites rather than confirmed top-selling-by-sales, which is itself part of the uncertainty). Opened /collections/must-haves/ and /collections/must-haves/?type=products directly and via a fresh session cookie jar: both return an HTML page titled 'HKLIVING: Login' containing only a dealer-login form (Username/Password/RememberMe fields, no __CategoryId hidden field, no article-list/product grid, no totalcount span) -- i.e. genuinely access-gated, not a rendering quirk. No site search endpoint was discoverable (input#searchField has no visible AJAX target in the static HTML; guessed /search/, /search?query=, and the known /umbraco/surface/... pattern all 404). No 'Bestsellers'/'Best Sellers'/'Top Sellers'/'Populair' wording found anywhere in nav, footer, or the collections index. Given the B2B/wholesale nature already established in the prior Home-Decor pass (no visible prices/checkout for normal visitors, but normal category browsing IS fully public), 'Must-haves' being gated while ordinary categories are not suggests it may be a dealer-exclusive curated list rather than a public bestsellers merchandising page -- recorded as a flagged manual-review candidate rather than silently dropped.
